counterfactual_missing_items: An incisional biopsy via anterior inferomedial transconjunctival orbitotomy was planned
normal anterior and posterior segment examinations without optic nerve signs
decisive_items: a large choroidal melanoma confirmed by histopathology and metastatic workup
MRI demonstrated a hyperintense mass on T1-weighted images and hypointense signal on T2-weighted images
response.rationale: C1 best integrates the prior choroidal melanoma with a new intraconal lesion showing intrinsic high-density areas and T1-hyperintense/T2-hypointense signal, strongly favoring orbital metastasis. R4 cavernous hemangioma is the main differential but is atypical given T2 hypointensity and intrinsic high-density areas, and it ignores the melanoma history. R7 is a correlated subset of C1 without the intrinsic high-density component; R3 and R2 are less supported or contradicted.

rejected.why: Superseded by C1; correlated subset lacking the intrinsic high-density areas component.
Only nonspecific well-defined intraconal lesion support; MRI signal and melanoma history favor metastasis.
Contradicted by normal anterior and posterior segment examinations and misidentifies the primary site as scleral rather than choroidal.
